searchText: Not sure if this is the right channel, but here's a question Why is EIP-712 not an ERC? It's not an improvement to Ethereum itself but a standard on top of it, similar to ERCs It is an ERC. Historically, all ERCs were EIPs. At some point people started calling contract standards ERCs, but they were still part of the EIP process and given an EIP number. People just called them "ERC-712" instead of "EIP-712" even those meant the same thing. More recently, the EIP and ERC repositories were split I believe, so now there are actually two separate processes, but 712 came before that. when searchingly for "erc 712" this pops up https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712 can't find it in ERCs either: https://github.com/ethereum/ERCs/tree/master/ERCS That is the correct link (first one). I don't think older ERCs were migrated to the new ERC repository. they were. EIP-712 is not in ERC category. it's under Standards Track > Interfaces (as opposed to Standards Track > ERC) i believe EIP editors consider it a mistake that it wasn't published in ERC category
